jordan: quick run summary — compared 65B q4f16 on h100 vs a100 across us-east1 / eu-west1 with the new kernel switcher. TL;DR: h100 wins latency & rps. p99 (seq256): h100=310ms, a100=380ms. per-GPU RPS (steady, concurrent=16): h100≈70 rps, a100≈55 rps. quant kernels reduce GPU mem by ~40% but add ~6% p99 on a100.

maya: nice — which model binary and quant config? and did you run the fallback kernels?

jordan: ran model: redwood/65b-v2, quant: q4f16 (LLM-quant v0.9), kernel policy: auto -> prefer-quant -> fp16-fallback. bench command: ```
# bench tool
bench --model redwood/65b-v2 --quant q4f16 --seq 256 --concurrency 16 --region us-east1,eu-west1 --jobs 300
```

oliver: for Dedicated sizing we need the straight RPS->GPU calc. give me the per-gpu effective capacity after headroom so we can turn this into commit numbers. also include a warmup spike estimate.

jordan: done. numbers below are steady-state. per-gpu RPS @concurrency16: h100=70 rps, a100=55 rps. recommended autoscale buffer: 25% (keep slots free for bursts/warmup). effective capacity per GPU = rps * 0.75. so for target 1000 rps: h100 gpus = ceil(1000 / (70*0.75)) = ceil(1000 / 52.5) = 20 GPUs. a100 gpus = ceil(1000 / (55*0.75)) = ceil(1000 / 41.25) = 25 GPUs.

ashley: note on warmup: observed a 3x token emission spike for first 60–90s after pool cold-start (KV warmup + embedding cache). that increases upstream rate and can trip autoscale if no buffer. recommend a small pre-warm job to populate prefix caches for top-100 prompts and keep a 20% warm-slot buffer for the first 2 minutes.

kevin: kernel fallback question — when quant kernel throws nan/overflow we fall back to fp16, right? any QoL regressions observed?

jordan: yes fallback -> fp16 kernel. fidelity: q4f16 caused ~0.8% of responses to change token-level output in our eval set (cr-2024-05-03-01). perceptible QA regressions were rare but present in corner cases (long instructions + tabular tokens). fallback path restored previous outputs in 95% of those cases.

ria: rollout plan suggestion: canary 5% traffic in us-east1 on h100, compare eval metrics (perp, exact-match) + live sampling for 24h, then 25% for 6h, then full. pin model version and quant flag per route so ops can yank quickly. add an alert for >1% drift in exact-match on the canary eval set.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: canary group (5%) -> 2024-05-04T02:00Z. CI: bench+eval + perf smoke.

maya: ok next steps: 1) jordan to create size proposal (h100 vs a100) with cost delta 2) ashley to draft warmup playbook 3) ria to create canary eval dashboard. I'll slot a 30m sync tomorrow. :+1:

jordan: will post the size proposal doc (numbers + cost) by EOD and add the bench logs + perf CSVs.

oliver: sounds good. remember to include cross-region cold-start penalties (eu-west1 p99 ~ +20ms to us-east1) in SLA math.

ashley: also include a recommended burst-slot approach: keep 10 ephemeral warm slots per pool for the first 120s after incident-fallbacks.

kevin: noted. if regression >1% on canary, auto-roll back and tag for model-qa.

maya: thanks all — saving notes here for the sizing ticket.
